headline: New York City and Los Angeles, the two largest US school districts, have restricted student use of AI, though AI is now built into many ordinary school tools.
score_reason: Policies were announced in early September, so the news is stale; kept as context.
importance_line: Millions of students face limits on AI in school, but the limits are hard to enforce because AI features sit inside common tools like Canva and PowerPoint.
source: The Herald Insight, citing Education Week
summary: The Herald Insight reports, relaying Education Week, that New York City announced on 2 Sep 2026 a one-year moratorium on student use of generative AI from pre-K to grade 8, while Los Angeles Unified restricted AI on district-owned devices for this school year. Education researchers quoted say it is hard to separate AI from ordinary software such as Canva and PowerPoint, which makes restrictions difficult to apply.
notes: Older news (2 Sep 2026) re-dated; the Education Week original was not read.
